def: An open protocol that lets AI applications discover and use tools, resources and prompts from servers through a common set of JSON-RPC messages.
The application the user runs, which owns the model conversation, chooses what the model may see and asks the user for approval.
A component inside a host that keeps one connection to one MCP server.
A program, local or remote, that exposes tools, resources and prompts over MCP.
A small standard for remote procedure calls in JSON, made of requests with ids, responses holding a result or an error, and one-way notifications.
An MCP transport in which the client launches the server as a subprocess and exchanges newline-delimited JSON-RPC messages over its standard input and output.
An MCP transport using a single HTTP endpoint where each client message is a POST and the server replies with JSON or a Server-Sent Events stream.
The exchange during initialisation in which client and server declare which optional features they support and agree to use only those.
A model-controlled function offered by a server, listed with tools/list and run with tools/call.
Data identified by a URI that a server offers as context, chosen by the host application and fetched with resources/read.
A reusable message template offered by a server and invoked explicitly by the user, fetched with prompts/get.
The flag on a tools/call result that marks a tool execution failure the model can read and correct, as opposed to a protocol error.
Hiding malicious instructions in a tool description or result so that the model follows them.
